issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the reference solution specify Stock.take(String) returning an int (returning -1 on failure and remaining quantity on success), but the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) with a boolean return type. This mismatch will confuse students implementing SealSaloon and inventory logic (e.g., calls expecting an int result) and prevents following the specification and solution behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template's Stock.take(String) method signature and implementation to return an int (like the UML and solution): return -1 if the ingredient is missing or out of stock, otherwise decrement quantity and return the new quantity. This aligns the template with the problem specification and the reference solution.

issues.description: The Stock.take method is conceptually the same across artifacts but is declared with different return types: the problem statement (UML) and the solution expect take(String) to return an int (using -1 to signal failure), while the template Stock class declares take(String) returning boolean. This mismatch of the same conceptual method name and expected semantics creates a mapping and compilation confusion for students implementing SealSaloon, who will rely on the int-return contract described in the task and used in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution: change the template Stock.take(String) signature to return int and implement the same contract as the UML/solution (return -1 when the ingredient is missing or out of stock, otherwise decrement quantity and return the remaining quantity). Update any template code comments or usages accordingly so students can directly follow the task description.
